messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: High tail latency detected on model-serving-prod (p99 > 2s for 6m). Auto-pager to #eng-oncall. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/alerts/1765439999 :rotating_light:

lucy: grabbing the pager. initial glance: spike correlated with KV cache evictions on pool-eu-central-1. Streaming clients showing chunk gaps ~1-2s.

tom: I'm seeing a particular pattern: large number of short-lived prefill writes from conversation-summarizer service pushing thousands of tiny keys. KV write throughput is fine but free contiguous blocks are fragmented.

maya: logs sample: ```
2026-03-14T21:45:12Z worker-22: decode_latency_ms=2300 kv_miss=true rehydrate_ms=1800
2026-03-14T21:45:13Z worker-22: prefill_write_size_bytes=128 prefill_key_count=3200
```

jess: no deploys reported. infra-bot: No infra changes in last 2h.

kevin: hypothesis: the prefill workload is creating a high volume of small KV entries that cause allocator fragmentation; during decode we need large contiguous KV ranges which now get evicted or require multi-chunk reads causing stalls.

lucy: mitigation plan brainstormed: A) throttle prefill for the offending producer, B) increase eviction threshold temporarily, C) enable per-request KV pinning to keep decode keys resident, D) fall back streaming to non-streaming short-context path for affected customers.

maya: I'm going to throttle the prefill producer by applying a rate limit: `k8s scale prefill-producer -n prod --replicas=1` and also add ingress QoS.

infra-bot: ACTION: scaled prefill-producer down to 1 replica.

jess: immediate effect: KV eviction_rate down ~50% after 45s, p95 improved from 700ms to 420ms, p99 still elevated ~1.6s. Some streaming stalls still visible from earlier requests that need rehydration.

kevin: enable pinning for active sessions on pool-eu-central-1: `kvctl pin --pool pool-eu-central-1 --mode active-sessions`. This will reserve recently used KV extents for in-flight decodes. Small risk to capacity for new requests.

infra-bot: START: pinning enabled on canary nodes pool-eu-central-1-canary-1..2.

infra-bot: SUCCESS: pinning canaries show reduced rehydrate_count and p99 on canaries dropped to ~700ms. Rolling to full pool.

lucy: rolling pin to all nodes.

infra-bot: DONE: KV pinning enabled on pool-eu-central-1. Monitor memory headroom.

jess: after these steps p95=350ms p99=620ms and streaming gap counts back near baseline. Still seeing a small tail from requests that hit storage backend due to multi-chunk reassembly. Those are being processed.

support: received 14 customer tickets reporting slower streaming responses in the last 30m; no 5xxs. Flagging high-usage customers A, B for follow-up.

kevin: medium-term actions: 1) change allocator to prefer larger contiguous allocations for decode-heavy models, 2) introduce prefill scoring so only high-value prefixes are prefilled, 3) add fragmentation metric and alert to tie p99 regressions to fragmentation.

lucy: temp rollback steps in case of regression: revert pinning, scale prefill-producer back to previous replicas, reduce cache_quota if memory becomes constrained.

jess: will author incident ticket and attach timeline + mitigations: https://incident.redwood/incidents/2026-03-kv-frag-001

maya: handoff  my shift ends in 12m. lucy will own post-incident follow-up. lucy, anything else?

lucy: I'll watch for reoccurrence for next 2 hours and coordinate with eng-ml for prefill scoring design. kevin please prioritize allocator experiment.

kevin: acknowledged, adding allocator task to eng-runtime sprint and will prototype contiguous-first allocator in a hotfix branch.

support: drafting customer note: brief incident summary + actions taken, promise full RCA in 48h.

incident-bot: RESOLVED: SLOs recovered to baseline. Auto-pager closed.

lucy: added follow-ups: `RCA owner=lucy, allocator owner=kevin, prefill scoring owner=tom, support_comm=support`. Will include sample traces in RCA. Marking thread resolved. :white_check_mark:
